title: Bijectivity of the normalized affine resolution section class
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes, $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, $I$ an injective resolution of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $p\in\mathbb N$, and $V\subset S$ an affine open. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $M=F|_U$ and $P=R^p f_*F$, where cohomology and ordinary higher images are right derived functors [pqf-def-cohomology]. Let $R$ be any augmentation-preserving restricted resolution section data [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Then the specified additive class map $c:H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,M)\to\Gamma(V,P)$ is bijective, where $c$ is resolutionSectionClass for $R$, followed by evaluation at $V$ of the inverse of $I.\mathrm{isoRightDerivedObj}(f_*,p)$. The class map sends the cohomology class of a cocycle of the restricted resolution to the section of the homology sheaf it defines [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. No Ext comparison is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tags 01F4 (2), 01XJ (1), 01E4 and 01E5; affine degeneration and normalization on cocycles

proof.text: Put K=f_*I. Every term K^n has vanishing positive module cohomology on V because direct images of injective modules are section-acyclic. Identify H^n(K) with R^n f_*F using I.isoRightDerivedObj. Ordinary higher-image quasi-coherence transports along this isomorphism and persists under open restriction. Affine vanishing, transported from H to module right-derived sections by the source comparison, gives positive cohomology vanishing for H^n(K)|V.

Apply the general acyclic section/homology comparison to K,V,p. Expanding resolutionSectionClass expresses it as a composite of the restricted resolution cohomology isomorphism, exact additive forgetting, homology of R.sections, exact presheaf evaluation, and the now-invertible theta component. Hence it is an isomorphism. Evaluation of the inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj is also an isomorphism. Their composite is bijective in AddCommGrpCat. Only R.sections being an isomorphism is needed for bijectivity; the augmentation and component equations are unnecessary.
